questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that Australia was so far away and that I would probably not have a similar chance of staying there for an extended period after I finished my studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information was easy to obtain, although the host university office always took some time in replying to personal inquieries.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A couple of introductory sessions, which were very basic, non-social stuff that was for the most part unnecessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Options were quite extensive. Most exchange students lived on campus, which was nice. There are over a dozen different accommodations to choose from.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Only the undergraduate housing had meal plan options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Live on campus, it's much nicer and easier to meet new people. Go to Fenner, a lot of exchange students went there and liked it. I stayed at Yukeembruk, which had the most exchange students, but also many unsociable people from Asia, so it did not have a great community vibe to it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Prices for accommodations were insane, but that's the case everywhere in AUS.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Took some steps, but you work yourself through.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emailing the host university, which took a while to respond.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Registration was easy. Even after classes had started I shifted my courses around quite a bit, which was nice.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The course level was fairly easy I have to say. Considering they were master classes, I got through most of them with little effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's similar, although there are much more students in classes and lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Foreign Policy Analysis
Foundations of Finance
The Resort to Force
Strategic Diplomacy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the courses were quite interesting. I would recommend the course Foreign Policy Analysis the most, as the professor was extremely engaging and knowledgable, and the weekly topics were interesting and time-relevant. Foundations of Finance was quite hard, as I had never completed a finance course before, but I wanted to challenge myself a bit, so I got what I was looking for. Also had a great professor. the other two courses were also recommendable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travelling the country was more expensive than anticipated, but obiously worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer was quite expensive if bought in supermarkets or liquor stores. Other alcohol in student bars was quite cheap during happy hours tho.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of clubs and associations to join. Definetly join something to meet new people.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports between the accommodation halls (football, australian rugby, volleyball). Also running club which hosts a iron-man style run at the end of the semster.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do a sport or attend a non-sport club to make new friends or for free meals/beers. I went to a few German society meetings and it was fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Tasmania is great, but if you are there during winter the weather will be absolutely freezing. Otherwise, New Zealand is so worth it! East coast trip during the mid-sem break is also very popular among exchange students, but having your own car or renting one is very recommendable for all these destinations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Many Aussies at uni are quite young (18-21), as they start higher education right away and most do not persue a masters degree, because it is too expensive. As a master student, most of my classmates were from Asia and did not speak English well or sometime at all, so it was hard to make same aged Aussie friends for me. I got a job at the local irish pub tho, and got some more Aussie contact through that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Very heavy Asian influence on campus, the supermarkets and restaurants on campus made it feel a bit like studying in Beijing at times lol.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The close and compact style of the university grounds, and the laid back atmosphere everyday.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would not go to Canberra/ANU tbh. It is not by the beach and the weather there gets really cold. It was a good experience but I would not particularly recommend it, since there are other universities in cities that are much nicer (Sydney or Melbourne). 
Bring warm clothes if you do go there, but make it stuff you can leave behind, so you travel easier on your post-study travels.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: travelling after the semester had ended. New Zealand, East Coast, Vietnam.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The cold weather and the fact that I did not particularly fancy Canberra as a city.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
